text.p: French aluminium and packaging giant Pechiney said on Monday that it expected to post a second-half loss in 1996.

"The last quarter of the year will show a marked deterioration of (the company's) results and in these conditions, the net result of the second half, which showed a profit of about 100 million francs in 1995 (on a proforma basis) should produce a loss," the company said in a statement.

The company said its 1996 results would be affected by exceptional provisions, of which the most important would be related to the Challenge project, as well as the consequences of a court action about patents brought by American National Can, for which a definitive judgement has not yet been announced.
The company did not give a specific forecast for 1996 results.
It said the second-half loss was caused by the absence of a rebound in its principal markets as well as a deterioration of volumes in drink can sales in the United States and Europe.
The company the rise of the dollar and the increase in global demand for aluminium would only help the company after the first months of the year.

"The encouraging signs at the end of the year, such as the level of worldwide demand for aluminium and the rise of the dollar, will have effect, if they are confirmed, only after the first few months of 1997," the company said.
